goal_en: Talk about your job and where you live, using regular verbs.

scene.setting_en: Emma starts work at the hospital in Freising. Her boss, Dr. Anna Schmid, welcomes her.

lines.speaker: dr_schmid
lines.de: Guten Morgen, Frau Clarke! Willkommen im Team.
lines.en: Good morning, Ms Clarke! Welcome to the team.

lines.speaker: emma
lines.de: Guten Morgen, Frau Dr. Schmid! Ich freue mich.
lines.en: Good morning, Dr Schmid! I'm happy to be here.

lines.speaker: dr_schmid
lines.de: Sie arbeiten hier als Krankenschwester, richtig?
lines.en: You're working here as a nurse, right?

lines.speaker: emma
lines.de: Ja, genau. In England arbeite ich auch im Krankenhaus.
lines.en: Yes, exactly. In England I also work at a hospital.

lines.speaker: emma
lines.de: Ich wohne in Marzling. Ich fahre mit der S-Bahn.
lines.en: I live in Marzling. I take the S-Bahn.

lines.speaker: dr_schmid
lines.de: Prima! Wir beginnen um acht Uhr. Und jetzt zeige ich Ihnen die Station.
lines.en: Great! We start at eight. And now I'll show you the ward.

vocabulary.example_de: Die Arbeit beginnt um acht Uhr.

vocabulary.note_en: The official job title today is 'Pflegefachfrau' / 'Pflegefachmann'. Note: no article before jobs: 'Ich bin Krankenschwester.'

vocabulary.example_de: Die Station ist im ersten Stock.
vocabulary.example_en: The ward is on the first floor.

grammar.title_en: Regular verbs in the present tense
grammar.explanation_en: Most German verbs follow one pattern. Take the infinitive (wohnen), remove -en to get the stem (wohn-) and add the ending for each person. Verbs with a stem ending in -t or -d add an extra -e- for du and er/sie/es: 'du arbeitest', 'sie arbeitet'. In a normal statement the verb is always in second position.

examples.en: In England I work too. (verb stays in second position)

exercises.prompt_en: Choose the right form: 'Emma ___ in Marzling.'
Put the words in the right order. Start with 'Jetzt'.
Listen and type what you hear.
Match the German and English words.

dialogue.setting_en: Lukas visits his brother at the hospital and meets you in the cafeteria.

turns.speaker: lukas
turns.de: Hallo Emma! Mein Bruder arbeitet auch hier. Arbeitest du gern hier?
turns.en: Hi Emma! My brother works here too. Do you like working here?

options.feedback_en: Great! 'gern' after the verb means you like doing it.
That means 'I live in the hospital'. Use 'arbeiten' for work.

options.de: Ich wohne in Marzling, du weißt doch!
options.feedback_en: Ha, exactly! Lukas knows that already.
Lukas asked where you live, not where you work.

turns.speaker: lukas
turns.de: Stimmt! Bis morgen in der Bäckerei!
turns.en: True! See you tomorrow at the bakery!
